description: Curated list of the most frequently asked DSA questions in placement and technical interviews. Each entry includes a problem description, a sample test case, and a reference Java solution with time and space complexity.

questions.title: Two Sum
questions.description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. Each input has exactly one solution and the same element cannot be used twice.

testCase.explanation: nums[0] + nums[1] = 2 + 7 = 9, so return indices 0 and 1.

questions.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
questions.description: You are given prices where prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i. Buy on one day and sell on a later day to maximize profit. Return the max profit, or 0 if no profit is possible.

testCase.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price=1) and sell on day 5 (price=6), profit = 6 - 1 = 5.

questions.title: Product of Array Except Self
questions.description: Given an array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] equals the product of all elements of nums except nums[i]. Solve without using division and in O(n) time.

questions.title: Maximum Subarray (Kadane's Algorithm)
questions.description: Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return that sum.

testCase.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2,1] has the largest sum = 6.

questions.title: Merge Intervals
questions.description: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals and return the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the input intervals.

testCase.explanation: [1,3] and [2,6] overlap, so they merge into [1,6].

questions.title: Container With Most Water
questions.description: Given n non-negative heights, each representing a vertical line, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding the most water. Return the maximum area.

testCase.explanation: Lines at index 1 (h=8) and index 8 (h=7) give area = min(8,7) * (8-1) = 7 * 7 = 49.

questions.title: 3Sum
questions.description: Given an integer array nums, return all unique triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i, j, k are distinct and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0. The solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.

testCase.explanation: Two distinct triplets sum to 0: (-1,-1,2) and (-1,0,1).

questions.title: Trapping Rain Water
questions.description: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

testCase.explanation: Water gets trapped in the valleys between taller bars, totalling 6 units.

questions.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
questions.description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring that contains no repeating characters.

testCase.explanation: The longest substring without repeats is "abc", which has length 3.

questions.title: Valid Parentheses
questions.description: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid. Brackets must close in the correct order and every opening bracket must have a matching closing bracket.

testCase.explanation: Every bracket is closed by the same type in the correct order, so the string is valid.

questions.title: Group Anagrams
questions.description: Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together. Two strings are anagrams if one can be formed by rearranging the letters of the other.

testCase.explanation: Strings sharing the same sorted letters are grouped together.

questions.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
questions.description: Given a string s, return the longest substring of s that is a palindrome.

testCase.explanation: "bab" is a palindrome of length 3 ("aba" is also a valid answer).

questions.title: Reverse Linked List
questions.description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the new head.

testCase.explanation: Each node's next pointer is reversed so the list runs backwards.

questions.title: Linked List Cycle
questions.description: Given the head of a linked list, determine if the list has a cycle in it (a node that can be reached again by continuously following the next pointer).

testCase.input: head = [3,2,0,-4], cycle connects tail to node index 1
testCase.explanation: The tail's next points back to the node with value 2, forming a cycle.

questions.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
questions.description: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list by splicing together their nodes. Return the head of the merged list.

testCase.explanation: Nodes from both lists are interleaved in sorted order.

questions.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
questions.description: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth (the number of nodes along the longest path from the root down to the farthest leaf).

testCase.explanation: Longest root-to-leaf path is 3 -> 20 -> 15 (or 7), giving depth 3.

questions.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
questions.description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values (from left to right, level by level).

testCase.explanation: Nodes are grouped by depth: level 0 = [3], level 1 = [9,20], level 2 = [15,7].

questions.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
questions.description: Given a binary search tree (BST), find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of two given nodes p and q. The LCA is the lowest node that has both p and q as descendants (a node can be a descendant of itself).

testCase.explanation: Nodes 2 and 8 are on opposite sides of the root 6, so 6 is their LCA.

questions.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
questions.description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the length of the diameter: the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes. This path may or may not pass through the root.

testCase.explanation: Longest path is 4 -> 2 -> 1 -> 3 (or 5 -> 2 -> 1 -> 3), which has 3 edges.

questions.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
questions.description: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST). For every node, all values in the left subtree must be smaller and all values in the right subtree must be larger.

testCase.explanation: Left child 1 < 2 and right child 3 > 2, so the tree is a valid BST.

questions.title: Number of Islands
questions.description: Given an m x n 2D grid of '1's (land) and '0's (water), return the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and formed by connecting adjacent land cells horizontally or vertically.

testCase.explanation: One island is the connected block of land in the top-left; the single land cell at bottom-right is the second.

questions.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
questions.description: Given a sorted array that has been rotated at an unknown pivot and a target value, return the index of target if it is present, otherwise return -1. Must run in O(log n) time.

testCase.explanation: Value 0 is located at index 4 in the rotated array.

questions.title: Climbing Stairs
questions.description: You are climbing a staircase that takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can climb either 1 or 2 steps. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.

questions.title: House Robber
questions.description: You are a robber planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has some money, but you cannot rob two adjacent houses (alarms connect them). Return the maximum amount you can rob without alerting the police.

testCase.explanation: Rob house 0 (2) + house 2 (9) + house 4 (1) = 12.

questions.title: Longest Common Subsequence
questions.description: Given two strings text1 and text2, return the length of their longest common subsequence. A subsequence keeps relative order but need not be contiguous. Return 0 if there is none.

testCase.explanation: The longest common subsequence is "ace" with length 3.

questions.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
questions.description: Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

testCase.explanation: The longest increasing subsequence is [2,3,7,101], which has length 4.

questions.title: Subsets
questions.description: Given an integer array nums of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set). The solution set must not contain duplicate subsets.

testCase.explanation: All 2^3 = 8 subsets of the three elements are returned.

questions.title: Permutations
questions.description: Given an array nums of distinct integers, return all possible permutations in any order.

testCase.explanation: All 3! = 6 orderings of the three elements are returned.

questions.title: Combination Sum
questions.description: Given an array of distinct integers candidates and a target, return all unique combinations where the chosen numbers sum to target. The same number may be chosen unlimited times.

testCase.explanation: 2+2+3 = 7 and 7 itself both reach the target.
